artboards.title: Cell by cell: shipped vs proposed

annotations.text:
Review: dates

1. The Date column prints the stored CHAR(8) value (20260904). Missed Trips and the Dispatch Log already format service dates; this module is the odd one out.
2. Scheduled and Actual repeat the month and day in every row, and format in the viewer's browser time zone. The service date is agency-local, so for anyone outside Central the two columns can disagree across midnight. Format in America/Chicago and show time only.
3. Fixed Route sorts by severity first, then date, so the Date column does not run in order and a trend cannot be read off the table. Proposed: group by service day, severity within the day.
4. Today is never settled (the candidate poll judges a run only after its service day ends at 01:20). Today's rows should say so instead of looking like clean departures.
5. The window offers no per-day view. The strip above the table shows reviewable departures per service day with weekends marked.

Review: operators and vehicles

Fixed Route: operator_name arrives as "LAST, FIRST -badge" in capitals and is printed as-is. Split the badge into a monospace reference and case the name. vehicle_label is a fleet number and is already right.

On-Demand: driver_id and vehicle_id are Spare UUIDs (spareApi.ts: "Driver and vehicle are ids, never names"). Both print as 36-character strings under headers that promise a driver and a vehicle. Show an eight-character reference with the full id on hover, and say in the header that it is a Spare reference. duty_identifier silently falls back to the raw duty id; label the fallback.

Terminology: Fixed Route says Operator, On-Demand says Driver. The contract says operator. Use one word.

Both views: blank is rendered as a dash. "No operator on record" and "No vehicle on record" are what the reviewer needs to know.

Grouping by operator or vehicle (segmented control in the toolbar) is what turns the log into an assessment tool: repeat offenders surface with a count and an average, sorted worst first.

Review: correct behaviour and contract compliance

1. The "Late pullouts" card counts pullout_status = 'Late Relief'. complianceCandidatesPoll.ts documents that Late Relief is a mid-shift driver changeover, never emitted by the feed in 22 days of data. That card is 0 forever.
2. statusClass() colours Expired Pullout red and Late Relief amber; Missed Pullout, Missed Login and Late Pullout (408 runs that never left, per the same file) render as neutral grey pills.
3. The summary applies no variance, while the candidate rule applies 10 minutes and a settled-day guard. The module's numbers do not match what becomes a compliance occurrence. Proposed: an Outcome column and cards that apply the same rule, with the allowance printed in the toolbar.
4. Avail's status is kept as its own column, shown as emitted, because it is evidence; Outcome is the judgement.
5. On-Demand already has the right shape (Source, Outcome, allowance in the card label). The proposal brings Fixed Route up to it and shows the scheduled and actual source under the time instead of an asterisk footnote.

Behind these mockups

- One agency-local formatter (America/Chicago) for service day and times, shared with the Dispatch Log and Missed Trips rather than a fourth copy.
- Group by operator/vehicle and the per-day strip can be computed client-side from the rows already returned; nothing new from the API.
- Outcome for Fixed Route reuses garageDepartureCandidatePredicate() logic; expose settled_before and variance in diagnostics so the console cannot drift from the poll.
- On-demand names need a Spare driver and vehicle directory sync (identifier, licence plate). Until then the short reference is the honest display.
- Sample data on these artboards is invented: fictional operators, plausible blocks and fleet numbers, Spare-style ids. Counts in the cards and the strip are illustrative.
